title: Q–Q plot as a named distributional display
dek: Wikipedia Q–Q: sample quantiles versus theoretical quantiles. Genomic inflation is a GWAS costume of the same idea.
story: A Q–Q plot on Wikipedia compares quantiles of a sample to quantiles of a reference law (often Normal, or Uniform for p-values). Points on the diagonal mean 'this reference is a plausible bulk'.
GWAS λ_GC is a median-based summary of a χ² Q–Q. A skyline Manhattan without a Q–Q is incomplete; a Q–Q with λ=1.5 and a pretty skyline is a structure warning (stats-gwas).
Residual Q–Q in OLS is stats-ols-diagnostics territory. This card is the encyclopedia display name.
deep: Tails are noisy; a few off-diagonal points can be discoveries or bad QC.
Plotting −log10 p Q–Q emphasises tails on purpose.
A straight line with slope ≠1 is a scale problem, not a mean problem.
Do not 'correct' a Q–Q by deleting the peak SNPs and declaring victory without a scientific null.

visual.caption: Schematic: a reference law versus a sample that is overdispersed in the tail (inflation). Q–Q would bow off the diagonal even if the means match.
